question: Which of the following microfinance units were established in India at the time of independence?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rural Cooperatives**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Rural Cooperatives were one of the earliest forms of microfinance institutions established in India.
 
• They were set up to provide credit and financial services to rural and agricultural sectors.
 
• The aim was to eliminate the exploitation by moneylenders and to provide farmers with access to necessary financial resources.
 
• These cooperatives played a crucial role in the development and upliftment of rural areas post-independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Grameen Model Banks**

 
 
• This model was popularized by Muhammad Yunus in Bangladesh and is not originally from India.
 
• It focuses on group-based lending and has been adapted in various parts of the world.
 
 
 
• **Joint Liability Groups (JLGs)**
 
 
• Introduced much later as a microfinance model to provide loans based on group guarantees.
 
• They are aimed at ensuring credit access to small farmers and rural entrepreneurs.
 
 
 
• **Self Help Groups (SHGs)**
 
 
• These were introduced in India in the 1980s and gained popularity in the 1990s.
 
• SHGs are small groups of people who come together to save and lend to each other.
 
• They are often linked with banks for larger financial support.
 
 
 
• **Cooperative Societies Act**
 
 
• In India, the first Cooperative Societies Act was passed in 1904.
 
• This act laid the foundation for the cooperative movement in India.
 
• The act aimed at providing a legal framework for cooperative societies.
